title: Optimized FusX Assembly Technique for Mitochondrial Variations in Human Cell Lines
author: Kar, Sabharwal, et al.
materials:
Timing: ∼1 week
6.Cell culture.The protocol described below provides the steps for maintaining HEK293T cells, including how to start a cell culture from frozen vials of cells in cryogenic storage. Similar procedures can be used for HT1080 cells as well.a.Thaw cryopreserved cells by putting the cryogenic vials in a 37°C water bath. Spray the thawed vial with 70% ethanol and wipe carefully to reduce the possibility of contamination. Transfer thawed liquid contents into a 10 mL conical tube prefilled with 9 mL fresh complete culture medium (DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% Pen-Strep).b.Collect cells for plating.i.Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the cells in 1 mL of fresh DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% Pen-Strep.ii.Plate ∼1–2 × 106 cells in a T75 flask and incubate cultures at 37°C.c.Passage the HEK293T cells upon 80%–90% confluency (it usually takes 4–6 days). Subculture ratio is 1:10.Note: Culture medium should be prewarmed to 37°C before use.
7.Cell preparation for transfection.a.Cell dissociation before plating.i.Discard culture medium and subsequently rinse the adhered cells with PBS. Aspirate PBS and add 3 mL 0.25% Trypsin solution (with EDTA) to the T-75 flask and incubate at 37°C for ∼5 min.ii.Tap the flask gently on the side to dislodge the cells completely and add 7 mL of DMEM to the flask to deactivate the Trypsin. Transfer the cells to a 15 mL conical tube (Tube A).iii.Count the cells/mL by using a hemacytometer.Alternatives: Automated cell counters such as ThermoFisher Scientific Countess 3 FL Automated Cell Counter (Catalog# AMQAF2000) can be used for cell counting.b.Seeding of cells at a suitable density.i.Typically, for the base editing experiments in a 6-well plate, take 18 mL of DMEM in a 50 mL conical tube and add media from tube A containing ∼1.8 × 106 cells. Mix the sample gently and transfer about 3 mL of media into each well (∼0.3 × 106 cells/well). Incubate cells at 37°C for 14–16 h in 5% CO2 incubator. The number of 6-well plates can be scaled up according to the needs of the experiments.ii.By the next day, the cells should be at 70%–80% confluent in each well and ready for transfection.Note: To save time, cell culture and seeding can be started ahead of time so that plasmids can be transfected immediately after sequence verification.Note: Alternatively, cells can be seeded on 24 or 48-well plates. Seeding density should be adjusted accordingly.
8.Transfection with FusXTBE plasmids.The following steps describe the detailed procedures for using Lipofectamine 3000 to transfect HEK293T cells with the FusXTBE left and right arms plasmid DNA.a.Add 1.2 μg (0.6 μg per arm) of FusXTBE plasmid DNA to a microcentrifuge tube, adjust the volume to 122 μL with Opti-MEM and add 3 μL of P3000 Reagent.b.Add 120 μL Opti-MEM and 5 μL lipofectamine 3000 to a separate microcentrifuge tube.c.Mix the contents of both tubes thoroughly by pipetting up and down. Spin briefly.d.Incubate the transfection mix at room temperature (∼25°C) for 10–15 min.e.Add the transfection mix to the cells dropwise, swirl the plate to evenly distribute the mixture, and incubate the cells for at 37°C.f.After 10 h of transfection, exchange media with fresh culture medium.Note: The aforementioned transfection protocol is suitable for a single well from a 6-well plate (with a surface area of 9.6 cm2). If larger or smaller wells are used, the recipe should be adjusted accordingly.g.Harvest cells 4–6 days post transfection for genomic DNA isolation.Pause point: The cells can be stored at −80°C until genomic DNA isolation.Note: Transfection of each pair of FusXTBE plasmids should be done in triplicate.Note: Untransfected control (wild type) should be set up and cells should be collected. We recommend setting up a positive transfection control by transfecting with a GFP plasmid for easy transfection confirmation.Note: The amount of plasmid DNA used may need to be decreased or increased to achieve the best editing efficiency.

steps.title: Prepare LB liquid media
steps.instruction: Add 25 g of commercial LB broth powder to 950 mL of water, dissolve, bring the volume to 1 L and autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min (liquid cycle). Aliquot the sterile LB, store at 4 °C for up to 6 months, bring aliquots to room temperature (~25 °C) and add kanamycin and spectinomycin to a final concentration of 50 µg/mL before using for primary culture.

steps.title: Prepare LB agar plates
steps.instruction: Add 15 g of agar powder to 1 L of the prepared LB liquid media and autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min (liquid cycle). Cool the molten agar to ~50–55 °C, add kanamycin and spectinomycin (final 50 µg/mL), mix well, and pour ~25 mL into each petri dish. Allow plates to solidify at room temperature (~25 °C). Store plates at 4 °C for up to 60 days.

steps.title: Prepare 0.3 M IPTG stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 714.93 mg of IPTG in 8 mL of Nanopure water, bring the volume to 10 mL with Nanopure water, filter‑sterilize through a 0.22 µm filter, aliquot into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 20 mg/mL X‑Gal stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 200 mg of X‑Gal in 8 mL of N,N‑dimethylformamide, bring the volume to 10 mL with the same solvent, aliquot into amber glass or polypropylene vials and store at –20 °C. Handle kanamycin, spectinomycin, IPTG and X‑Gal with gloves; they are harmful if inhaled/ingested and may irritate skin.

steps.title: Thaw and start primary cell culture
steps.instruction: Place a cryogenic vial of HEK293T (or HT1080) cells in a 37 °C water bath until thawed, spray the vial with 70 % ethanol and wipe. Transfer the cell suspension to a 10 mL conical tube containing 9 mL fresh complete DMEM (10 % FBS, 1 % Pen‑Strep). Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL fresh complete DMEM, and plate 1–2 × 10⁶ cells in a T75 flask. Incubate at 37 °C; pre‑warm culture medium to 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Passage cells to maintain confluency
steps.instruction: When cultures reach 80–90 % confluency (typically 4–6 days), passage the cells at a 1:10 split ratio using the same trypsinization procedure described below.

steps.title: Dissociate, count, and seed cells for transfection
steps.instruction: Discard medium, rinse adherent cells with PBS, aspirate PBS, add 3 mL of 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA to the T75 flask and incubate at 37 °C for ~5 min. Tap the flask gently to detach cells, add 7 mL DMEM to neutralize trypsin, and transfer the suspension to a 15 mL conical tube (Tube A). Count cells using a hemacytometer or an automated counter. For a 6‑well plate, mix ~1.8 × 10⁶ cells (from Tube A) with 18 mL DMEM in a 50 mL tube, then dispense ~3 mL (~0.3 × 10⁶ cells) into each well. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 14–16 h. The next day cells should be 70–80 % confluent and ready for transfection. Scale the volume proportionally for additional plates or for 24‑/48‑well plates, adjusting seeding density accordingly.

steps.title: Transfect cells with FusXTBE plasmids
steps.instruction:
For each well of a 6‑well plate (surface area 9.6 cm²):
1. Add 1.2 µg total FusXTBE plasmid DNA (0.6 µg per arm) to a microcentrifuge tube, bring the volume to 122 µL with Opti‑MEM and add 3 µL P3000 reagent.
2. In a second tube, mix 120 µL Opti‑MEM with 5 µL Lipofectamine 3000.
3. Combine the contents of the two tubes, mix by pipetting up/down, and spin briefly.
4. Incubate the transfection mixture at room temperature (~25 °C) for 10–15 min.
5. Add the mixture dropwise to the cells, swirl the plate to distribute evenly, and incubate at 37 °C.
6. After 10 h, replace the medium with fresh complete DMEM.
Adjust reagent volumes proportionally for larger or smaller wells. Perform each plasmid pair transfection in triplicate, include an untransfected wild‑type control and a GFP‑plasmid control for transfection efficiency. DNA amount may be titrated to optimise editing.

steps.title: Harvest cells for genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Four to six days after transfection, collect cells for genomic DNA isolation. Cells may be stored at –80 °C until DNA extraction.
